headline: China's chip exports nearly doubled to $177 billion in H1 2026 96% year-on-year increase
summary: China's chip exports surged 96% year-on-year to $177 billion in H1 2026, driven by global demand for AI hardware and memory price boom.
details: China exported 179.44 billion integrated circuits worth $177.28 billion in the first six months of 2026, an increase of more than 96% year on year by value, according to data released by the country's General Administration of Customs.

caption:
China's chip exports nearly doubled to $177 billion in H1 2026. What's driving this surge?

China exported 179.44 billion integrated circuits worth $177.28 billion in the first six months of 2026, an increase of more than 96% year on year by value, according to data released by the country's General Administration of Customs.

The customs administration attributed the surge to global demand for AI hardware, but the underlying numbers point more towards a worldwide memory price boom that has inflated the value of the commodity-grade chips that China exports in volume.

The half-year value figure implies an average of roughly $0.99 per exported chip, which reflects the composition of China's IC exports: memory, power management, microcontrollers, and other mature-node parts, along with chips packaged and tested in China for re-export.
